main_task: Open a new presentation and insert a title slide with a title and subtitle
main_steps: Click the title text box and type “Designing a presentation”.
Click the subtitle text box and type “Master slides and styles”.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on New Slide in the Presentation toolbar.  
2. In the slide layout that appears, select a title slide.  
3. Type the title in the title text box.  
4. Type the subtitle in the subtitle text box.

main_task: Open the Master Slides deck in the Sidebar
main_steps: Click the Sidebar toggle if the Sidebar is not visible.
Click the Master Slides deck icon in the Sidebar.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
- Open the Sidebar
- Locate the Master Slides deck in the Sidebar
- Click the expand marker next to the "Used in This Presentation" panel to view master slide thumbnails (if needed)

main_task: Create a new master slide and rename it to “Company Master”
main_steps: Click View on the menu bar.
Click New Master on the Master View toolbar.
Click Rename Master on the Master View toolbar.
Type Company Master in the Name text box.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on New Master in the Master View toolbar.  
2. Right-click on a master slide in the Slides pane and select New Master from the context menu.  
3. Click on Rename Master in the Master View toolbar.  
4. Right-click on the new master slide in the Slides pane and select Rename Master from the context menu.  
5. Enter "Company Master" in the Name text box.  
6. Click OK to save the changes and close the dialog.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a selected drawing object to use for creating a custom style
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle onto the blank slide.
Resize the rectangle so it is clearly visible.
Click the rectangle to select it.
main_task: Create a new custom drawing style from the selected object
main_steps: Open the Styles deck on the Sidebar.
Click Drawing Styles at the top left of the Styles deck.
Click New Style from Selection at the top right of the Styles deck.
Click the Enter new style name text box.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select an object in the presentation.
2. Open the Styles deck on the Sidebar by clicking on Styles or by using the keyboard shortcut F11 (macOS ⌘+T).
3. Click on Drawing Styles in the Styles title bar to open the Drawing Styles panel.
4. Click on New Style from Selection on the right side of the Styles deck title bar.
5. Enter a name for the new custom drawing style in the Enter new style name text box.
6. Click OK to save the new drawing style.

main_task: Open the Templates dialog and set a presentation template as the default template
main_steps: Click File on the menu bar.
Select a presentation template in the Templates dialog.
section_path: Chapter 2, Master Slides, Styles, and Templates
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Go to File > New > Templates on the menu bar to open the Templates dialog.  
2) Select the presentation template to set as the default from the list.  
3) Right-click on the selected template and choose Set as Default from the context menu.  
4) Click Open to confirm and create a new presentation using the new default template. The default template is now set for future presentations.

main_task: Create a horizontal text box using the keyboard shortcut F2
main_steps: Click on the blank slide canvas.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
- Press F2 to insert a horizontal text box.

main_task: Create a text box and apply a visible border, then set its text to two columns
main_steps: Click the Insert Text Box tool on the Standard toolbar.
Click and drag on the slide to draw a text box.

Type the text “If you are using a vertical text box, it is the height that will increase as a single line when you enter text. If you click and drag using vertical text box, you set the height of the text box and the width of the text box automatically increases creating multiple vertical lines.”
Click the text box border to select it.
Right-click the text box border and click Line.
Enter a line width greater than 0.35 cm.
Right-click inside the text box and click Text Attributes.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Insert a text box.  
2. Click in the text box to select it and display the selection handles.  
3. Right-click in the text box and select Text Attributes from the context menu to open the Text dialog.  
4. Click on Text Columns in the Text dialog to open the Text Columns page.  
5. Set the number of columns in the Number of columns box.  
6. Set the spacing between columns in the Spacing box.  
7. Click OK in the Text dialog to save changes and close it.  
8. Click outside the text box to deselect it.

main_task: Insert a special character into a text box
main_steps: Create a text box on the slide.
Click inside the text box so the text cursor is visible.
Place the cursor after the space.
Click Insert on the menu bar.
Select the character “€” in the special characters dialog.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click at the position in the text where the special character is to be inserted.  
2. Go to Insert > Special Character on the menu bar to open the Special Characters dialog.  
3. Select the font and character subset from the Font and Character drop-down lists.  
4. Locate and select the desired special character from the available characters; the character appears in the preview box.  
5. Click Insert to insert the character at the cursor position and close the dialog.  
Alternatively, double-click the selected character to insert it and close the dialog.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with a text box containing a sample paragraph
setup_steps: Insert a new text box on the blank slide.
Type the text "Direct formatting can be applied to characters words and sentences." into the text box.
main_task: Open the Character dialog and apply character formatting to the word “characters”
main_steps: Select the word “characters” in the text box.
In the Character dialog, open the Fonts page if needed.
Change the font size to 32 pt.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the word "characters" in the text box.  
2. Open the Character dialog by right-clicking on the selected text and choosing "Character" from the context menu, or by going to Format > Character on the menu bar.  
3. Use the formatting options in the Character dialog to apply desired character formatting.  
4. Click OK to save the changes and close the dialog.  
5. Click outside the text box to deselect it.

main_task: Create a bulleted list in a text box and change one list point to a lower outline level
main_steps: Create a new text box on the slide.
Click Toggle Unordered List on the Text Formatting toolbar.
Press Shift and Tab at the same time to decrease the indent level of the third list point.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on the text box and type the first list item, then press Enter to create a new list point.  
2. Type a second list item and press Enter to create another list point.  
3. Click on the second list point (the one you want to change).  
4. Press the Tab key to demote that list point to a lower outline level.

main_task: Create a horizontal text callout and enter text in it
main_steps: Click the Callouts for horizontal text tool on the Text toolbar.
Click and drag on the slide to draw a callout.
Click a blank area on the slide.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Click on "Callouts" on the Text toolbar to select the horizontal text callout tool.  
2) Click in the slide and drag to create the callout.  
3) Double-click in the callout box to enter text mode.  
4) Type the required text.  
5) Click in a blank space in the slide to save the changes and exit text mode.

main_task: Insert a fixed date field into the slide
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. In the slide, go to the master slide or the slide where the field is to be inserted.  
2. Click on the "Insert" menu and select "Date (fixed)" to insert a fixed date field.  
3. Right-click on the inserted date field and select the desired date format from the context menu.  
4. Confirm the selection to apply the format.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a blank slide with a text box containing a web address
setup_steps: Insert a new text box on the slide.
Type “https://example.com” into the text box.
main_task: Create a hyperlink from the web address using the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+K
main_steps: Select the text “https://example.com” in the text box.
Press Ctrl and K at the same time.
In the Hyperlink dialog, keep the web type selected and click Apply.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Press Ctrl+K to open the Hyperlink dialog.  
2. Enter the web address in the URL text box.  
3. (Optional) Enter a name in the Text text box if desired.  
4. Press Enter or click OK to create the hyperlink.

main_task: Insert a document hyperlink into the current slide
main_steps: Open the Hyperlink dialog with Ctrl+K.
Click the Document type on the left side.
Click the Path text box and type /tmp/example.odt.
Click the Target text box and type Slide 2.
Click the Text text box and type Open document.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the slide where you want to insert the hyperlink.  
2. Go to Insert > Hyperlinks on the menu bar or press Ctrl+K (Windows) / ⌘+K (macOS).  
3. In the Hyperlink dialog, select "Document" from the left-hand type options.  
4. In the Path text box, enter the file path and document name in the format: file:///<path>/document_name.  
5. If linking to a specific slide in the document, enter the slide number or name in the Target text box or click "Target in Document" to select the target slide.  
6. Click Apply to insert the hyperlink into the slide.  
7. Click Close or OK to close the dialog.

main_task: Insert an image into the presentation using the Insert Image file browser
main_steps: In the file browser, navigate to the directory containing the image file.
If Preview is not selected, click Preview.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to Insert > Image on the Menu bar.  
2. Navigate to the directory containing the required image and select the file.  
3. Click on Open to place the image in the centre of the selected slide and close the file browser window.

main_task: Insert a gallery image onto the slide
main_steps: Click Insert on the menu bar.
Click the Diagrams theme in the Gallery deck.
Click and drag the top-left diagram image onto the slide.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on Gallery in the Sidebar.  
2. Select a theme from the available themes.  
3. Scroll through the images and select the required image.  
4. Click and hold the image, then drag it onto the slide. Release the mouse to insert the image centrally.

main_task: Create a new Gallery theme named “New Theme 1”
main_steps: Click Insert on the menu bar.
Click New at the bottom of the Gallery deck.
Click in the theme name text box.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on Gallery in the Sidebar.  
2. Click New at the bottom of the Gallery deck.  
3. Click on General in the Properties of New Theme dialog.  
4. Type "New Theme 1" in the text box.  
5. Click OK to save and close the dialog.

main_task: Crop the selected image using the Crop dialog and restore it with Original Size
main_steps: Click the image to select it.
Click Format on the menu bar.
Click in the Left value box.
Click in the Top value box.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select the image.  
2) Go to Format > Image > Crop Dialog.  
3) In the Crop dialog, click on Original Size.  
4) Click OK to save and close the dialog.

main_task: Open the ImageMap dialog for a selected image and apply a hotspot link
main_steps: Insert an image onto the slide and select it.
Click Tools on the menu bar.
Drag on the image to draw a hotspot.
Click in the Address field and type "https://example.com".
Click in the Text field and type "Example link".
Click the Frame drop-down and select "_self".
Click Save in the file browser.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select an image on a slide.  
2. Go to Tools > ImageMap to open the ImageMap dialog.  
3. Use the tools at the top of the dialog to define hotspots and assign links.  
4. Click Apply to apply the hotspot settings.  
5. Click Save to open the file browser and navigate to a folder for saving the image map.  
6. Enter a name for the image map.  
7. Click Save to save the image map.  
8. Click Close to close the ImageMap dialog.

main_task: Show the Drawing toolbar in Impress
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to View > Toolbars on the Menu bar.  
2. Select Drawing from the submenu to display the Drawing toolbar.

main_task: Show the Drawing toolbar
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to View > Toolbars on the Menu bar.  
2. Select Drawing from the submenu.

main_task: Draw a freeform line on the slide
main_steps: Click the triangle next to Curves and Polygons on the Drawing toolbar.
Click and hold on the slide.
Drag to draw a freeform line.
Release the mouse button to complete the drawing.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click the triangle ▼ next to Curves and Polygons on the Drawing toolbar.  
2. Select Freeform Line from the sub-toolbar.  
3. Click and hold the mouse button, then drag the cursor to draw the freeform line.  
4. Release the mouse button to complete the line.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with three separate shapes
setup_steps: Open a new blank slide.
Insert a rectangle on the left side of the slide.
Insert an ellipse on the upper right side of the slide.
Insert a diamond below the other two shapes.
main_task: Group the three shapes into one object
main_steps: Hold down the Shift key and click the rectangle.
Hold down the Shift key and click the ellipse.
Hold down the Shift key and click the diamond.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
- Select the three shapes to be grouped.
- Press Shift + G to group the selected shapes into a single object.

main_task: Rotate a selected graphic object using the quick rotation handles
main_steps: Click any graphic object on the slide to select it.
On the Line and Filling toolbar, click the triangle next to Transformations.
Click Rotate on the Transformations sub-toolbar.
Move the pointer over a corner selection handle.
Click and drag the corner handle to rotate the object.
Release the mouse button to finish the rotation.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the graphic object to rotate.  
2. Click the Rotate tool to enable rotation mode.  
3. The selection handles will change color and a pivot point will appear at the center of the object.  
4. Press and hold the Shift key to rotate the object beyond the defined rotation angle.  
5. Rotate the object to the desired angle and release the Shift key when complete.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with one rectangle
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle on the blank slide.
main_task: Open the Transformations toolbar and distort the rectangle with the Distort tool
main_steps: Click the rectangle to select it.
Click Distort on the Transformations toolbar.
Click Yes in the conversion dialog.
Drag a corner selection handle to distort the rectangle.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Open the Transformations toolbar.  
2. Click on the Distort tool.  
3. Select the rectangle.  
4. Click Yes to convert the object to a curve if prompted.  
5. Click and drag a corner selection handle to distort the rectangle using the opposite corner as an anchor point.  
6. Click and drag a vertical selection handle to distort the rectangle using the opposite vertical side as an anchor point.  
7. Click and drag a horizontal selection handle to distort the rectangle using the opposite horizontal side as an anchor point.

setup_task: Create two selectable objects on a blank slide
setup_steps: Insert a new blank slide.
Draw two separate rectangle objects on the slide.
main_task: Align the two rectangles to the left
main_steps: Click the triangle next to the Align Objects button.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the two rectangles.  
2. Right-click on the selected rectangles and choose Align Objects > Left.

setup_task: (Setup) Create two simple shapes on a blank slide
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle shape on the slide.
Insert a second rectangle shape on the slide.
main_task: Align the two rectangles to the left
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the two rectangles.  
2. Right-click on the selected rectangles and choose "Align Objects" from the context menu.  
3. Choose "Left" from the alignment options to align the left edges of the rectangles.

setup_task: (Setup) Create two overlapping shapes on a blank slide
setup_steps: Create a new blank slide.
Insert a rectangle shape on the slide.
Insert a circle shape so that it overlaps the rectangle.
main_task: Move the overlapping shapes backward or forward using Arrange
main_steps: Open Format > Arrange on the menu bar.
Click an arrange option that changes the selected shape's stack level.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
- Select the shape to move.
- Press Ctrl+Shift+→ (or ⌘+Shift+→) to move the selected shape forward.
- Press Ctrl+Shift+← (or ⌘+Shift+←) to move the selected shape backward.
- Alternatively, select the shape to move, then select the shape it should move in front of or behind, and click on it to swap positions.

main_task: Move a selected object behind all other objects using the Arrange menu
main_steps: Insert two overlapping shapes on the slide.
Click the front shape to select it.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Ensure the object to be moved is selected.  
2. Go to the Arrange menu.  
3. Choose "Send to Back" from the Arrange menu.

setup_task: (Setup) Create two overlapping objects on a blank slide
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle on the slide.
Insert a second rectangle that overlaps the first rectangle.
main_task: Move the selected rectangle in front of all other objects
main_steps: Click the back rectangle to select it.
Press Ctrl, Shift, and + at the same time.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Ensure the rectangle is selected.  
2. Press Ctrl+Shift++ (or ⌘+Shift++ on macOS) to bring the selected rectangle to the front of all other objects.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a simple drawing object to convert
setup_steps: Click the rectangle tool on the Drawing toolbar.
Draw a rectangle on the slide.
main_task: Convert the rectangle to a 3D object
main_steps: Click the rectangle to select it.
Go to Format > Convert on the menu bar.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
- Click on the rectangle object to select it.  
- Click the "Extrude" button (or toggle Extrusion) to convert the rectangle into a 3D object.

main_task: Assign a slide interaction to an object
main_steps: Draw a simple shape on the blank slide.
Open the Interaction dialog from the Format menu.
Click the Action at mouse click drop-down.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to View > Normal on the menu bar to open Normal view in the Workspace.  
2. Select the slide where you want to assign an interaction.  
3. Select the object (such as a button, image, or text) on the slide.  
4. Right-click the object and choose Interaction from the context menu, or go to Format > Interaction on the menu bar to open the Interaction dialog.  
5. In the Action at mouse click drop-down list, select the desired interaction.  
6. Click OK to save the changes and close the Interaction dialog.

main_task: Insert a Fontwork object and replace its default text with "Hello"
main_steps: Select a Fontwork style in the gallery.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to Insert > Fontwork on the menu bar to open the Fontwork Gallery dialog.  
2. Select a Fontwork style from the dialog and click OK. The Fontwork appears centrally on the slide.  
3. Double-click on the Fontwork text graphic to enter editing mode.  
4. Type "Hello" in the Fontwork text field to replace the default text.  
5. Press Esc or click outside the Fontwork graphic to confirm and finalize the text replacement.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with a text object for Fontwork
setup_steps: Insert a new text box on the blank slide.
Type “Impress Guide 7.5” into the text box.
main_task: Convert the text into Fontwork using the selected style and replace the default text with the prepared text
main_steps: Click Insert on the menu bar.
Press Ctrl and A at the same time.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to Insert > Fontwork on the menu bar to open the Fontwork Gallery dialog.  
2. Select a Fontwork style from the dialog and click OK. The selected Fontwork appears centrally on the slide.  
3. Double-click on the Fontwork text graphic to enter editing mode.  
4. Type the prepared text to replace the default text in the Fontwork graphic.  
5. Press the Esc key or click outside the Fontwork graphic to finalize the text replacement.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with a title and a text object for animation
setup_steps: Open a new blank presentation slide.
Insert a text box on the slide.
Type “Animated Text” in the text box.
main_task: Apply an animation effect to the text box and preview it
main_steps: Click the text box to select it.
Open the Animation deck on the Sidebar.
Select a category from the Category drop-down list.
Select an animation effect from the Effects list.
Click Play to preview the animation.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the text box containing the text to animate.  
2. Open the Text dialog and navigate to the Text Animation page.  
3. Choose an animation mode:  
   - All at once  
   - Word by word  
   - Letter by letter  
4. Enable the Automatic Preview option to see the animation effect in real time as it is applied.  
5. Click Apply to add the animation effect to the text box.  
6. The animation will be previewed automatically.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a line on a blank slide
setup_steps: Click the Line tool.
Drag on the slide to draw a straight line.
main_task: Format the selected line using the Line and Filling toolbar
main_steps: Click the line to select it.
Open the Line Style drop-down list and choose a dashed style.
Click the Line Width text box and type 0.05 cm.
Click the triangle to the right of Line Color and select a green color.
Open the left Arrow Style drop-down list and select an arrowhead.
Open the right Arrow Style drop-down list and select an arrowhead.
Click Shadow to turn on the shadow.
Click on an empty area of the slide to deselect the line.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Make sure a line is selected on a slide.  
2) Click on the Line Style drop-down list and select a line style.  
3) Type the desired line width in the Line Width text box, or use the up and down arrows to adjust the width.  
4) Click the triangle ▼ to the right of Line Color and select a color from the available palettes.  
5) If needed, select an arrowhead style from the left drop-down list to add an arrowhead at the start of the line, or from the right drop-down list to add an arrowhead at the end of the line.  
6) If necessary, click the Shadow button to apply a shadow using the current settings.  
7) Deselect the line to save the changes.

main_task: Create a new line style named “MyLineStyle” in the Line dialog
main_steps: Draw a line on the slide.
Select “Dots” in both Type drop-down lists.
Set Number to “3” in both Number fields.
Set Spacing to “20” in both Spacing fields.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Open the Line dialog by going to Format > Text Box and Shape > Line.  
2) Click on Line Styles to open the Line Styles page.  
3) In the Line style drop-down menu, select a predefined line style similar to the one you want to create.  
4) Click Add.  
5) In the Name dialog that opens, type "MyLineStyle" and click OK.  
6) In the Type drop-down list, select either Dots or Dash.  
7) In the Number field, specify the number of dots or dashes required.  
8) In the Length field, specify the length percentage for dashes (if Type is Dash).  
9) In the Spacing field, set the spacing percentage between dots and/or dashes.  
10) Optionally, check Fit to line width to ensure the style fits the line width.  
11) Click OK to save changes and close the Line dialog.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a rectangle to format with an area fill
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle on the blank slide.
main_task: Apply a solid color area fill to the rectangle using the Area dialog
main_steps: Open the Area dialog from Format > Text Box and Shape > Area.
Click the Area tab if it is not already open.
Open the Palette drop-down list and select libreoffice.
Click a blue color swatch in the palette.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the rectangle so that the selection handles are displayed.  
2. Open the Area dialog by right-clicking on the rectangle and selecting Area from the context menu.  
3. Click on Area to open the Area page.  
4. Click on Color to access color fill options.  
5. In the Palette drop-down list, select a color palette and choose a color from the available colors.  
6. Alternatively, enter RGB or Hex values in the text box or click Pick to select a color using the Pick a Color dialog.  
7. Click OK to save the changes and apply the solid color fill.

main_task: Apply a background image fill to the selected object
main_steps: Insert a shape onto the blank slide and select it.
Click anywhere outside the object to deselect it.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the object that will act as the window on the slide.  
2. Open the Area dialog and navigate to the Area page.  
3. Click on "Use Slide Background" in the Fill drop-down list or select it from the Area/Style Filling drop-down menu on the Line and Filling toolbar.  
4. The background image of the slide appears as a fill within the selected object, creating a window effect.  
5. If needed, deselect the object to finalize the background image fill.

setup_task: Create a simple shape to format
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle on the blank slide.
Keep the rectangle selected.
main_task: Apply a shadow to the selected rectangle using the Area dialog
main_steps: Click the bottom-right point in the position grid.
Open the Color drop-down list and select Blue Accent.
Click in the Distance box and type 5.50 mm.
Click in the Blur box and type 0 pt.
Click in the Transparency box and type 0%.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the rectangle.  
2. Click on Shadow in the Line and Filling toolbar.  
3. Ensure the Shadow option is selected in the Shadow page of the Area dialog.  
4. Adjust the shadow settings in the Area dialog, including transparency (0% to 100%).  
5. Deselect the rectangle to save the changes.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a rectangle object on the slide
setup_steps: Click the rectangle drawing tool.
Drag on the blank slide to draw one rectangle.
main_task: Apply a shadow to the rectangle using the Line and Filling toolbar
main_steps: Click the rectangle to select it.
Click Shadow on the Line and Filling toolbar.
Click on a blank area of the slide to deselect the rectangle.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the rectangle object.  
2. Click on Shadow in the Line and Filling toolbar.  
3. Adjust shadow settings (such as transparency) in the Shadow page of the Line dialog if needed.  
4. Deselect the rectangle to save the changes.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a text-containing object
setup_steps: Insert a text box on the slide.
Type the text “Sample text” in the text box.
Click outside the text box.
main_task: Set the text columns for the object to 2 columns with 0.5 cm spacing
main_steps: Open Format > Text Box and Shape > Text Attributes.
Type 2 in the Number of columns box.
Type 0.5 cm in the Spacing box.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click in the text object to select it, so that the selection handles are visible.  
2. Right-click in the text object and select "Text Attributes" from the context menu.  
3. In the Text dialog, click on "Text Columns" to open the Text Columns page.  
4. Enter "2" in the "Number of columns" text box.  
5. Enter "0.5" in the "Spacing" text box.  
6. Click OK to save the changes and close the dialog.

main_task: Add text columns to the selected object
main_steps: Select the object that contains text.
Enter 2 in the Number of columns box.
Enter 0.50 cm in the Spacing box.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click in the text box to select it, ensuring the selection handles are visible.  
2. Right-click in the text box and select Text Attributes from the context menu to open the Text dialog.  
3. Click on Text Columns in the Text dialog to open the Text Columns page.  
4. Enter the number of columns required in the Number of columns text box.  
5. Enter the spacing between columns in the Spacing text box.  
6. Click OK to save the changes and close the dialog.  
7. Click outside the text box to deselect it.

main_task: Open the Connector dialog and set connector spacing options
main_steps: Create a connector on the slide.
Open the Type drop-down list and select the first connector type shown.
Click the Line Skew field and type 0.
Click the Line Spacing field and type 0.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Right-click on a connector and select Connector from the context menu to open the Connector dialog.  
2) Select the type of connector from the Type drop-down list.  
3) Set the Line Skew to adjust the distance between connectors where multiple connectors overlap.  
4) Set the Line Spacing to adjust the horizontal and vertical space between the connector and the object at each end.  
5) Click OK to save the changes.

main_task: Open Slide Sorter view and the Slide Show Settings dialog
section_path: Chapter 9, Slide Shows and Photo Albums
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:

main_task: Change the callout style and spacing in the Position and Size dialog
main_steps: Open the Position and Size dialog.
Click the Extension drop-down and select Horizontal.
Click the Position drop-down and select Middle.
Click the Optimal checkbox to clear it.
Click a blank area on the slide.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the text callout so that the selection handles are displayed.  
2. Right-click on the selected text callout and choose Position and Size from the context menu.  
3. Click on the Callout tab in the Position and Size dialog.  
4. Select a callout style from Straight Line, Angled Line, or Angled Connector Line.  
5. In Spacing, enter the amount of space between the end of the callout line and the callout box.  
6. In Extension, select a drop-down option to define how the callout line extends from the callout box.  
7. In the By text box, enter a distance value to set the space between the start point of the connector line and the callout box.  
8. In the Position text box, select Top, Middle, or Bottom to position the start point of the connector line on the callout box.  
9. In Length, enter the length of the callout line segment from the callout box to the angle point of the connector line (if Angled Connector Line is selected and Optimal is not checked).  
10. Check the Optimal box to place the angle point at an optimal distance from the callout box (only available when Angled Connector Line is selected and Optimal is not selected).  
11. Click in a blank space on the slide to deselect the text callout and save the changes.

main_steps: Click the text box containing "Animation Demo".
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the text box containing the text to animate.  
2. Open the Text dialog and navigate to the Text Animation page.  
3. Choose an animation mode:  
   - All at once  
   - Word by word  
   - Letter by letter  
4. Enable the Automatic Preview option to preview the animation effect as it is applied.  
5. Click Apply to apply the animation effect to the text box.  
6. The animation will automatically preview in real time.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with a title and a graphic object
setup_steps: Create a new blank presentation slide.
Insert a text box on the slide and type “Green Bright”.
Insert a second object on the slide as a graphic or shape.
main_task: Add an animation effect to the selected object
main_steps: Select the graphic object on the slide.
Open the Animation deck on the Sidebar.
Open the Category drop-down list and select an animation category.
Open the Effects list and select an animation effect.
Open the Start drop-down list and select On click.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click "Add Effect" to add the selected object to the Animation preview box.  
2. Select an animation effect from the available options.  
3. Check "Automatic Preview" to automatically preview the animation effect when applied.  
4. Use the "After animation" drop-down to select what happens after the animation ends (e.g., "Don't dim", "Dim with color", "Hide after animation", or "Hide on next animation").  
5. Click "Options" to adjust animation timing and other settings.  
6. Click "Create" to insert the animation into the current slide.

main_task: Change a selected line using the Line and Filling toolbar
main_steps: Insert a line on the slide.
Click the line to select it.
Open the Line Style drop-down list and choose a dashed line style.
Click the Line Width box and type 0.10 cm.
Click the arrow next to Line Color and choose a visible color.
Open the left Arrow Style drop-down list and choose an arrowhead style.
Open the right Arrow Style drop-down list and choose an arrowhead style.
Click outside the line to deselect it.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Make sure a line is selected on a slide.  
2. Click on the Line and Filling toolbar.  
3. Select a line style from the Line Style drop-down list.  
4. Type a line width in the Line Width text box, or use the up and down arrows to adjust the line width.  
5. Click the triangle ▼ next to Line Color to open the color palette and select a color.  
6. If needed, select an arrowhead style from the Arrow Style drop-down lists: the left list adds an arrowhead to the start of the line, and the right list adds one to the end.  
7. Click OK in the Line dialog to save changes.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a line object to format
setup_steps: Draw a straight line on the blank slide.
main_task: Open the Line dialog and create a new line style named Triangle unfilled
main_steps: Go to Format > Text Box and Shape > Line.
Select a predefined line style from the Line style drop-down list.
Type Triangle unfilled in the Name dialog.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Open the Line dialog by going to Format > Text Box and Shape > Line.  
2) Click on Line Styles to open the Line Styles page.  
3) Click Add.  
4) Type "Triangle unfilled" in the Name dialog that opens.  
5) Click OK.  
6) Click OK to save any changes and close the Line dialog.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a rectangle to format
setup_steps: Draw a rectangle on the blank slide.
main_task: Apply a solid color area fill to the rectangle using the Area dialog
main_steps: Go to Format > Text Box and Shape > Area.
Click the Area tab if needed.
Open the Palette drop-down list and select LibreOffice.
Click the blue color swatch in the palette.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the rectangle so that the selection handles are displayed.  
2. Open the Area dialog by right-clicking on the rectangle and selecting Area from the context menu.  
3. Click on Area to open the Area page.  
4. Click on Color to access the color fill options.  
5. In the Palette drop-down list, select a color palette and choose a color from the available colors.  
6. Alternatively, enter the RGB or Hex value in the text box, or click Pick to select a color using the Pick a Color dialog.  
7. Click OK to save the changes and apply the solid color fill to the rectangle.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a slide with two overlapping rectangles for a background image fill exercise
setup_steps: Create a new blank slide.
Insert a rectangle.
Insert a second rectangle.
Move the second rectangle so it overlaps the first rectangle.
Select the top rectangle.
main_task: Apply the slide background as the fill of the selected top rectangle
main_steps: Click on the slide to deselect the rectangle.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the topmost rectangle in the stack of objects on the slide.  
2. Change the fill of the selected rectangle to "Use Slide Background" using one of the following methods:  
   - Open the Area dialog and select "Use Background" on the Area page, or  
   - On the Line and Filling toolbar, select "Use Slide Background" from the Area/Style Filling drop-down menu, or  
   - In the Area panel in the Properties deck on the Sidebar, select "Use Slide Background" from the Fill drop-down list.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a single shape to format
setup_steps: Insert a rectangle on the slide.
main_task: Apply a shadow to the rectangle using the Area dialog
main_steps: Click the center-right point in the position grid.
Open the Color drop-down and select Blue Accent.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Open the Area dialog by going to Format > Text Box and Shape > Area.  
2. Click on the Shadow tab in the Area dialog.  
3. Check the option "Use shadow" in the Properties section.  
4. Select a shadow position from the nine available positions.  
5. Choose a shadow color from the color palette in the Color drop-down list.  
6. Enter a distance value in the Distance box to offset the shadow from the rectangle.  
7. Enter a blur value in the Blur box (0 to 150) to adjust shadow softness.  
8. Enter a transparency percentage in the Transparency box (0% to 100%) to control opacity.  
9. Click OK to apply the shadow settings.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a simple shape to format
setup_steps: Open a blank Impress slide.
Insert a rectangle on the slide.
main_task: Apply a shadow to the rectangle and deselect it
main_steps: Click the rectangle to select it.
Click the Shadow button on the Line and Filling toolbar.
Click outside the rectangle to deselect it.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the rectangle.  
2. Click on Shadow in the Line and Filling toolbar.  
3. Ensure the "Use shadow" option is selected in the Shadow page of the Area dialog.  
4. Adjust the shadow transparency using the Transparency setting (0% to 100%).  
5. Deselect the rectangle.

main_task: Add text to a selected object and close text mode
main_steps: Insert a shape onto the blank slide.
Double-click the shape to enter text mode.
Click outside the shape to exit text mode.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click on the text frame to select it.  
2. Press F2 to switch to text edit mode and open the Text Formatting toolbar.  
3. Type the desired text into the selected text frame.  
4. Press Enter to confirm and exit text edit mode.

main_task: Open the Text Columns page for a text object and set it to 2 columns with 0.50 spacing
main_steps: Click the Number of columns text box and type 2.
Click the Spacing text box and type 0.50.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Click in the text object to select it and display the selection handles.  
2. Right-click in the text object and select Text Attributes from the context menu to open the Text dialog.  
3. Click on Text Columns to open the Text Columns page.  
4. Enter 2 in the Number of columns text box.  
5. Enter 0.50 in the Spacing text box.  
6. Click OK to save the changes and close the Text dialog.

main_task: Create a new custom drawing style from the Sidebar and leave it unlinked
main_steps: Create a new graphic object on the slide.
Open the Styles deck on the Sidebar.
Click Drawing Styles in the Styles title bar.
Right-click a selected drawing style in the list.
Click New on the context menu.
Click the Name text box and type Untitled1.
Click the Inherit from drop-down list and select None.
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Open the Styles deck on the Sidebar by clicking on Styles at the side of the Sidebar.  
2) Click on Drawing Styles in the Styles title bar to open the Drawing Styles panel.  
3) Right-click on a drawing style in the list and select New from the context menu to open the Graphic Styles dialog.  
4) Enter a name for the new drawing style in the Name text box.  
5) In the Inherit from text box, select None from the drop-down list to ensure the new style is not linked to any existing style.  
6) Use the various pages in the Graphic Styles dialog to format the new style as needed.  
7) Click OK to save the new drawing style.

main_task: Open Slide Sorter view and the Slide Show Settings dialog
section_path: Chapter 9, Slide Shows and Photo Albums
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to View > Slide Sorter on the Menu bar to open the Slide Sorter view.  
2. Go to Slide Show > Slide Show Settings on the Menu bar to open the Slide Show Settings dialog.

main_task: Create a custom slide show with the name “Demo Show” and add the first two slides in order
main_steps: In the Existing slides box, click the first slide.
Hold Shift and click the second slide.
section_path: Chapter 9, Slide Shows and Photo Albums
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to Slide Show > Custom Slide Show on the menu bar to open the Custom Slide Shows dialog.  
2. Click on New to open the Define Custom Slide Show dialog.  
3. Enter "Demo Show" in the Name text box.  
4. In the Existing slides box, select the first slide and hold down the Shift key, then click the second slide to select both in sequence.  
5. Click on >> to move the selected slides to the Selected slides box.  
6. Rearrange the slides in the Selected slides box so that the first slide appears first, followed by the second slide.  
7. Click OK to close the Define Custom Slide Shows dialog.  
8. Click Start in the Custom Slide Shows dialog to test the custom slide show.  
9. Click OK to save the custom slide show and close the dialog.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a simple presentation with two slides
setup_steps: Click the new presentation option to start a blank presentation.
Insert a second slide.
main_task: Apply a slide transition to the first slide and preview it
main_steps: Click the first slide in the Slides pane.
Click the Slide Transition deck in the Sidebar.
Select the Variant drop-down list and choose the first available option.
Click the Sound drop-down list and select “No sound”.
Select the On mouse click option under Advance Slide.
section_path: Chapter 9, Slide Shows and Photo Albums
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Open the presentation file.  
2. In the Slides pane or Slide Sorter view, select the first slide.  
3. Click on "Slide Transition" in the Sidebar to open the Slide Transition deck.  
4. Click on a transition from the displayed list to apply it to the selected slide.  
5. In "Modify Transition", select an option from the drop-down list.  
6. In "Advance Slide", select "Automatic Preview" to preview how the transition looks.

main_task: Apply and then remove an animation on a selected slide object
main_steps: Click View on the menu bar.
Select a slide element on the slide.
Select Entrance in the Category drop-down list.
Select Venetian Blinds in the Effect drop-down list.
Select On click in the Start drop-down list.
Select Vertical in the Direction drop-down list.
Enter 0.50 sec in the Duration box.
Enter 3.0 sec in the Delay box.
section_path: Chapter 9, Slide Shows and Photo Albums
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the slide object to which you want to apply an animation.  
2. Choose an animation effect from the available options.  
3. Select the direction from the drop-down list to define how the animation appears.  
4. Select the after animation effect from the drop-down list (e.g., Don't dim, Dim with color, Hide after animation, Hide on next animation).  
5. Click Create to insert the animation into the slide.  
6. To remove the animation, select the same slide object.  
7. Choose the animation effect again and select "None" from the effect options.  
8. Click Create to remove the animation.

main_task: Apply the specified entrance animations to two selected objects and rehearse the timings
main_steps: Select the first object on the slide.
Hold Shift and select the second object on the slide.
Click Add Effect to open the animation options.
Select the first element (Shape 1) in the Animation deck.
Open the Category drop-down list and select Entrance.
Select the second element (Shape 3) in the Animation deck.
Open the Category drop-down list and select Entrance.
Click Slide Show on the menu bar.
section_path: Chapter 9, Slide Shows and Photo Albums
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select the first object.  
2. Choose "Entrance" from the Category drop-down list.  
3. Set Duration to 0.50 sec.  
4. Set Delay to 3.0 sec.  
5. Select the second object.  
6. Choose "Entrance" from the Category drop-down list.  
7. Set Duration to 0.50 sec.  
8. Set Delay to 3.0 sec.  
9. Enable "Automatic Preview" to preview the animation effects.

main_task: Create a photo album from the first slide
main_steps: Click the first slide in the presentation.
section_path: Chapter 9, Slide Shows and Photo Albums
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Select the first slide in the presentation.  
2) Go to Insert > Media > Photo Album.  
3) Click Add to open the file browser.  
4) Navigate to the folder containing the photographs.  
5) Select the photographs and click Open.  
6) In the Slide layout drop-down list, select the number of images per slide.  
7) If desired, select Add caption to each slide to insert a text box for captions.  
8) If only one image per slide is used, select Fill Screen to fill the entire slide.  
9) Arrange the photographs in the desired sequence by moving them up or down in the list.  
10) Click Insert Slides to create the slides for the photo album.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a presentation with one photo album slide
setup_steps: Open a new presentation.
Click the first slide.
Click Insert on the menu bar.
Click Media.
Click Photo Album.
Click Add.
Select one photograph file in the file browser.
Click Open.
Click Insert Slides.
main_task: Add a soft frame to the photograph using the Effect panel
main_steps: Click the photo on the slide.
Open the Properties deck on the Sidebar.
In Glow, click the Radius box.
In Glow, click the Color drop-down list.
In Glow, click the Transparency box.
In Soft Edge, click the Radius box.
section_path: Chapter 9, Slide Shows and Photo Albums
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Select a slide in the photo album to open the Image, Line, and Effect panels in the Properties deck on the Sidebar.  
2. In the Effect panel, adjust the following options to add a soft frame:  
   – Glow Radius: set a radius value to apply a soft frame around the photograph.  
   – Glow Color: select a color from the available color palettes for the soft frame.  
   – Glow Transparency: enter a transparency value to adjust the transparency of the soft frame.  
   – Soft Edge Radius: adjust the radius value to reduce the internal width of the soft frame and make the photograph look smaller.

main_task: Open the LibreOffice Options dialog and show the User Data page
main_steps: Click Tools on the menu bar.
Click the expansion marker next to LibreOffice in the left pane.
section_path: Chapter 11, Setting Up and Customizing Impress
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1) Go to Tools > Options (macOS LibreOffice > Preferences) on the Menu bar to open the Options LibreOffice dialog.  
2) Click the expansion marker next to LibreOffice on the left-hand side and select User Data to open the User Data page.

main_task: Change the LibreOffice print options to print transparency warnings
main_steps: Open the Tools menu and click Options.
In the left panel, expand LibreOffice and click Print.
In Warnings, click the Transparency checkbox.
section_path: Chapter 11, Setting Up and Customizing Impress
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Open the Print dialog in LibreOffice.  
2. Navigate to the Transparency section.  
3. Select the "Transparency" option to enable a warning when transparencies are contained in the document.  
4. If prompted, choose how to handle the transparency in the dialog that appears.

main_task: Open the LibreOffice Impress options dialog and enable grid display settings
main_steps: Click the expansion marker next to LibreOffice Impress in the left-hand pane.
section_path: Chapter 11, Setting Up and Customizing Impress
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Go to Tools > Options > LibreOffice Impress > Grid (macOS: Preferences > LibreOffice Impress > Grid).  
2. In the Grid dialog, select the "Visible grid" option.  
3. Click OK to apply the settings.

main_task: Open the Impress print settings and enable Hidden pages with Black & white quality
main_steps: Open the LibreOffice Impress Options dialog.
In the left pane, click "LibreOffice Impress".
Under Print, click the checkbox for "Hidden pages".
section_path: Chapter 11, Setting Up and Customizing Impress
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Open the Print dialog in LibreOffice Impress.  
2. Click on "More options" to access additional printing settings.  
3. In the Print dialog, ensure that "Contents" is selected so that hidden pages are included.  
4. In the Print dialog, select "Black & white" under the Color option.

main_task: Open the LibreOffice extension repository website
section_path: Chapter 11, Setting Up and Customizing Impress
relevant_procedure:
Relevant procedure:
1. Open the default browser.  
2. Navigate to https://extensions.libreoffice.org/.
